name: IEC NAND gate (rectangular form)
summary: IEC AND box with a negation circle or polarity triangle at its output, giving the NAND function.
description: In the IEC rectangular system there is no separate NAND qualifier. The element is an & box whose output carries a logic negation circle, or in data-book practice a polarity triangle marking the output as active-low. The output therefore stands at its external 0 state only when all inputs are active.

When reading device data books that use polarity indicators instead of circles, the triangle at the output means the internal 1 state produces a low level. A drawing should be consistent: mixing circles and triangles on the same sheet invites misreading because circles depend on the declared logic convention.
The symbol does not show output drive type. Open-collector, three-state or totem-pole outputs need their own qualifier inside the outline next to the output line.
readingNotes: Look for the circle or triangle at the output edge; it is easy to miss on a reduced print.
Confirm whether the sheet uses positive logic, negative logic or polarity indicators.
drawingChecklist: Draw the negation mark touching the outline at the output.
State the logic convention in the sheet notes.
Add an output-type qualifier where the output is not a standard push-pull stage.
distinction: An & box with a negated input rather than a negated output is a different function (an inhibit-type AND), not a NAND.
